title: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B: Agentic coding power, now open to all
description: Alibaba released Qwen3.6-35B-A3B as an open model focused on agentic coding capabilities. Hacker News discussion highlights its performance in coding tasks and comparison with proprietary models like Claude Opus 4.7.
author: Alibaba Qwen Team

title: Codex for almost everything - OpenAI announcement
description: OpenAI announced expanded capabilities for Codex, positioning it as a solution for 'almost everything' in software development. Hacker News discussion raises questions about overhype and practical limitations.
author: OpenAI

title: Android CLI: Build Android apps 3x faster using any agent
description: Google announced Android CLI, a command-line interface that enables AI agents to build Android apps 3x faster. Hacker News discussion explores implications for mobile development and agent workflows.
author: Google

title: The future of everything is lies, I guess: Where do we go from here?
description: Kyle Kingsbury (Aphyr) discusses the implications of AI-generated content on truth and trust. Explores the concept of 'meat shields' - humans accountable for AI systems - and the broader societal impact of AI-generated falsehoods.
author: Kyle Kingsbury (Aphyr)

title: Claude Opus 4.7 release discussion on Hacker News
description: Hacker News discussion about Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.7 release. Users discuss capabilities, pricing, performance improvements, and comparisons with other models like GPT-5.4 and open-source alternatives.
author: Hacker News Community

title: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on my laptop drew me a better pelican than Claude Opus 4.7
description: Simon Willison compared two major model releases from April 16, 2026: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B from Alibaba and Claude Opus 4.7 from Anthropic, using his 'pelican riding a bicycle' benchmark. The local Qwen model produced better results than the premium Claude Opus model, highlighting the growing capabilities of open/local models.
author: Simon Willison

title: Release: llm-anthropic 0.25 with Claude Opus 4.7 support
description: New release of llm-anthropic plugin adding support for Claude Opus 4.7 with thinking_effort: xhigh parameter, new thinking_display and thinking_adaptive boolean options, and increased default max_tokens to maximum allowed for each model.
author: Simon Willison

title: datasette.io news preview tool built with Claude Artifacts
description: Simon used Claude Artifacts to build a custom preview UI for datasette.io news section, taking advantage of Claude's ability to clone GitHub repos and examine content. Demonstrates vibe coding with Claude for building developer tools.
author: Simon Willison

title: TREX: Automating LLM Fine-tuning via Agent-Driven Tree-based Exploration
description: Research paper introducing TREX, a system that automates LLM fine-tuning using agent-driven tree-based exploration. Addresses the challenge of automating the fine-tuning process for large language models through intelligent exploration strategies.
author: Zerun Ma, Guoqiang Wang, Xinchen Xie, et al.

title: Memory Transfer Learning: How Memories are Transferred Across Domains in Coding Agents
description: Research paper investigating how coding agents transfer memory across different domains. Explores memory mechanisms that enable AI coding agents to apply learned knowledge from one domain to solve problems in another domain.
author: Kangsan Kim, Minki Kang, Taeil Kim, et al.

title: WebXSkill: Skill Learning for Autonomous Web Agents
description: Paper presenting WebXSkill, a framework for learning skills that autonomous web agents can use. Addresses the challenge of enabling web agents to acquire and reuse skills for autonomous web navigation and interaction tasks.
author: Zhaoyang Wang, Qianhui Wu, Xuchao Zhang, et al.

title: From Feelings to Metrics: Understanding and Formalizing How Users Vibe-Test LLMs
description: Research paper studying how users perform informal 'vibe testing' of LLMs and formalizing this process into measurable metrics. Addresses the gap between user intuition and formal evaluation methods for language models.
author: Itay Itzhak, Eliya Habba, Gabriel Stanovsky, Yonatan Belinkov

title: Gemini 3.1 Flash TTS with prompt-directed voice generation
description: Google released Gemini 3.1 Flash TTS, a text-to-speech model that can be directed using detailed prompts. Simon experimented with directing accents and characteristics, finding the prompting approach surprisingly verbose but effective at generating different regional accents.
author: Simon Willison

title: Datasette 1.0a27 replaces CSRF tokens with Sec-Fetch-Site headers
description: Major Datasette update replacing Django-style CSRF form tokens with modern browser headers (Sec-Fetch-Site) based on Filippo Valsorda's research. Also introduces RenameTableEvent for table rename operations and new actor parameter for client methods.
author: Simon Willison

title: OpenAI announces GPT-5.4-Cyber model and Trusted Access program
description: OpenAI released GPT-5.4-Cyber, a variant fine-tuned for defensive cybersecurity use cases, extending their Trusted Access for Cyber verification program. Appears to be a response to Anthropic's Claude Mythos and Project Glasswing.
author: Simon Willison

title: Cybersecurity Looks Like Proof of Work Now
description: UK's AI Safety Institute evaluation of Claude Mythos shows that more tokens spent equals better security results. Drew Breunig notes this creates an economic incentive: to harden a system you need to spend more tokens discovering exploits than attackers will spend exploiting them. Makes open source libraries more valuable as security investment can be shared.
author: Simon Willison (citing Drew Breunig)

title: Claude Code redesign focuses on managing multiple AI agents
description: Anthropic redesigned Claude Code desktop app with focus on managing multiple AI agents simultaneously. New features include sidebar for session management, drag-and-drop layout customization, built-in terminal, and file editor.
author: Emma Roth, The Verge

title: Gemini with Personal Intelligence rolling out globally
description: Google's Gemini Personal Intelligence feature, which pulls information from Gmail, Photos, Search, and YouTube history, is rolling out globally except UK, Switzerland, and EEA. Initially available for paid subscribers before free users.
author: Emma Roth, The Verge

title: Chrome now lets you turn AI prompts into repeatable 'Skills'
description: Google added AI Skills feature to Chrome, allowing users to save AI prompts as reusable workflows. Skills can be shared and used across different contexts, representing a shift toward prompt-based automation.
author: Tom Warren, The Verge

title: Steve Yegge vs Google on AI adoption rates
description: Heated exchange between Steve Yegge (claiming Google has low AI adoption similar to John Deere) and Google engineers Addy Osmani and Demis Hassabis (disputing the claims, stating 40K SWEs use agentic coding weekly). Highlights industry-wide AI adoption patterns: 20% agentic power users, 20% refusers, 60% using chat tools.
author: Simon Willison

title: Exploring the new servo embeddable browser engine crate
description: Simon investigated the new servo v0.1.0 crate, an embeddable browser engine for Rust. Built a CLI tool 'servo-shot' for taking screenshots using servo. Found that compiling Servo to WebAssembly isn't feasible due to heavy thread usage, but built a playground for html5ever/markup5ever WebAssembly builds.
author: Simon Willison

title: Bryan Cantrill on LLMs and the virtue of laziness
description: Bryan Cantrill argues that LLMs lack the virtue of laziness - work costs nothing to an LLM, so they don't optimize for future time by creating crisp abstractions. Human laziness forces us to develop good abstractions to avoid wasting our own time. LLMs left unchecked will make systems larger, not better.
author: Bryan Cantrill (cited by Simon Willison)

title: Audio transcription with Gemma 4 E2B and MLX
description: Simon shared a recipe for transcribing audio files on macOS using the 10.28 GB Gemma 4 E2B model with MLX and mlx-vlm using 'uv run'. Demonstrates local model usage for speech-to-text tasks with good results.
author: Simon Willison

title: SQLite 3.53.0 with ALTER TABLE constraints and query formatting
description: SQLite 3.53.0 release adds ALTER TABLE support for adding/removing NOT NULL and CHECK constraints, new json_array_insert() function, and significant CLI improvements including a new Query Results Formatter library. Simon compiled the formatter to WebAssembly and built a playground interface.
author: Simon Willison

title: Andrej Karpathy on the growing AI capability gap
description: Andrej Karpathy tweeted about the growing gap in AI capability understanding based on access points and domains. Notes that OpenAI's free Advanced Voice Mode runs on older GPT-4o era models while their highest-tier Codex model can spend 1 hour coherently restructuring entire codebases. Highlights that domains with explicit reward functions (coding, security) are improving faster due to RL trainability and B2B value.
author: Andrej Karpathy (cited by Simon Willison)
